The body is finely designed, and the inside of the resonance chamber is carefully carved to optimise the sound. The seven strings are of natural animal gut or plant fibre, with good elasticity and expressive tone. The pegs and the nut are of ivory or hardwood, for stability and durability. The whole structure combines traditional handwork with a national aesthetic.

The seven-string lyre comes from western Kenya and, over centuries of change and development, has become an important symbol of Luhya culture. 利通古琴音色溫潤而富有穿透力，兼具明亮與深沉的雙重特質。其七根琴弦在撥奏時發出清: The litungu's timbre is warm and penetrating, both bright and deep at once. Its seven strings give a clear, resonant sound when plucked, over a wide range, with a character of its own from the low fundamental to the high overtones. The resonance chamber of the body amplifies the string's sound wave effectively, so the tone projects well and sustains. Against the ornate refinement of the Western harp the litungu has a rawer, more rugged beauty; against the Asian guqin its sound is clearer and more direct, with a strong African character. Alternating strokes along the string with plucks produces complex, rich changes of tone, able to express tender, delicate feeling and to build a powerful, full-bodied atmosphere.
